correctness.rationale: The permanent is reconstructed exactly as the matrix coefficient of the normalized occupation-one vector in the irreducible \(U(n)\)-representation \(\operatorname{Sym}^n(\mathbb C^n)\). Its dimension is \(\binom{2n-1}{n}\), so Schur orthogonality gives the claimed second moment for every \(n\). Stirling and Markov then give the asymptotic ratio and probability bound. The bundled checker verifies the finite arithmetic independently; no experiment substitutes for the proof.

value.rationale: The discrepancy is exponential, not a cosmetic constant: it changes the full-Haar RMS scale and reverses the source’s anti-concentration conclusion at the quoted Gaussian-entry scale. The correction also clarifies an important ensemble distinction between a full Haar unitary and a small submatrix of a much larger Haar unitary. These are central quantitative claims in the paper’s main distribution and boson-sampling discussion.
